correctness.rationale: Every clique of the 3k-cycle power is in the consecutive-interval core or is one exceptional equilateral triangle. A good circular-arc cover and a degree-one radial map identify the core H1 as a primitive orientation line. Exactly k integral triangles attach with identical degree +1, so H2 is the augmentation kernel and all remaining reduced homology vanishes. Rotation preserves the oriented triangles; reflection reverses their orientation, and the equivariant relative boundary produces the full integral module and all traces. A separate exact finite verifier checks all faces in the declared ranges and signed Lefschetz numbers for all dihedral elements for k=2,...,8, but no finite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The 2011 source proves the nonequivariant k−1 two-sphere wedge, explicitly not a new claim here. The 2014 source establishes dihedral representations for the related but different circular-arc nerve; its Section 8 clique–nerve comparison does not preserve the full D_{3k} action due to different vertex counts. The 2015 source treats Rips homotopy transitions. Searches across equivalent terminology, an indexed literature corpus, and existing calculations did not reveal a covering integral signed dihedral action. A previously studied ordinary cyclic orbit space does not determine reflection parity or the full module. Residual risk: equivalent unindexed or implicit stronger equivariant treatment.

value.rationale: At the first canonical critical ratio 1/3, exceptional equilateral triangles create new two-dimensional homology. Its exact integral D_{3k}-module for every k>=2 is a natural structural invariant not fixed by the old wedge count. It determines reflection-sensitive parity and fixed-subgroup ranks, useful for symmetry quotients and coefficient changes, without claiming unproved downstream classifications.
